title: Structure and operating principles of a monkeypox virus replisome.
data_url: https://www.rcsb.org/structure/9NSP (plus PDB 10WP, 11WZ; EMDB EMD-49747, EMD-75504, EMD-76148)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Queried the RCSB PDB search API by this paper's DOI: it returns exactly 3 entries (10WP 'MPXV replisome bound to forked DNA', 6.5 Angstrom; 9NSP 'MPXV replisome bound to ssDNA', 4.1 Angstrom; 11WZ 'MPXV polymerase-E5 primase core complex', 3.8 Angstrom), all released 2026-09-02, each with one linked cryo-EM density map (EMD-49747, EMD-75504, EMD-76148). I downloaded 9NSP.cif (3.85 MB) and parsed it: 34,677 atoms, 6 chains, entities = 6 copies of E5 helicase-primase (uncoating factor OPG117), 1 DNA polymerase F8, 1 processivity factor OPG148 (A22), 1 uracil-DNA glycosylase (E4), one 13-nucleotide single-stranded DNA, one zinc ion. I ran a HEAD request on the EMD-49747 map: 479,759,383 bytes (480 MB) gzipped, which is over the 50 MB download cap.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The paper is not open access: Europe PMC reports isOpenAccess=N, inEPMC=N, no PMCID, hasSuppl=N, so there is no full text, no data availability statement and no supplementary file listing available to me. Everything about the biochemical assays, the single-molecule experiments and any Nature 'Source Data' files comes from the abstract alone; I never saw those numbers. The nature.com article page redirects to an authentication endpoint.

a1_downloadable.note: Partly. The 3 coordinate files and 3 maps are openly downloadable from RCSB PDB and EMDB with no login; I successfully pulled 9NSP.cif. The paper text and any Source Data tables are paywalled, so the assay measurements are not retrievable.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The deposited data is atomic coordinates and electron density maps. There is no outcome column anywhere. Any label a model could predict (helicase activity, primase activity, autoinhibited-versus-activated conformation, interface contacts) would have to be constructed by hand from figure panels in a paywalled paper.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs would be present in principle: full protein sequences are embedded in the mmCIF entity_poly records, so no accession lookups needed. But with only 3 structures this is moot.

a4_units_stated.note: Coordinates are in Angstroms and resolutions are stated in Angstroms in the PDB metadata (6.5, 4.1, 3.8). No measurement table with units exists to check.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, and this is the decisive one. The entire machine-readable output of this paper is 3 cryo-EM structures and 3 maps, verified by DOI search against the PDB. The checklist needs about 1,500 labelled rows, or 400 for classification. Three is three orders of magnitude short. The biochemical and single-molecule assays mentioned in the abstract are figure-level measurements on a handful of conditions, not a dataset.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~12 MB of coordinates if you take only the 3 mmCIF files; ~1.4 GB if you also take the 3 density maps (each about 480 MB gzipped, over the 50 MB per-file cap).
a6_fits_laptop.note: Coordinates fit trivially on a laptop. Maps exceed the download cap individually and would need a deliberate exception.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No disagreement found. The PDB citation records on all 3 entries point to this exact DOI and title, and the abstract's description (polymerase holoenzyme F8/A22/E4 plus E5 hexamer) matches the chain composition I parsed out of 9NSP.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL by absence rather than by circularity. There is no label to trace. If one invented a label such as 'activated versus autoinhibited conformation', it would be read off the same coordinates used as features, which is leakage by construction, exactly the A8 trap.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is possible: with 3 structures and no measured outcome column, any model would be fitting 3 examples and could claim nothing beyond them.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use viral replication-machine protein sequences and structures to predict whether the helicase switches into its active shape.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show a model the protein chains of the monkeypox virus replication machine (the E5 helicase-primase hexamer, the F8 polymerase, and the A22 and E4 processivity subunits) together with their three-dimensional coordinates. Verified example count: 3 structures.
plain_idea.predict: The output would be whether the helicase is in its switched-on or self-blocked shape, or how strongly it unwinds DNA. The true answer would come from the paper's own cryo-electron microscopy structures and its gel-based and single-molecule unwinding assays, none of which exist as a table.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Antiviral developers targeting poxvirus replication would want to know which contacts switch the helicase on, but a 3-example dataset cannot tell them; the structures themselves are useful to structural biologists directly, without any model.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper's data. The only machine-learning-shaped use of 3 cryo-EM structures is as a test case for an existing structure predictor, for example asking whether AlphaFold-Multimer or Boltz reproduces the E5-to-F8-thumb interface seen here. That is a one-afternoon anecdote on 3 complexes, not a project, and it needs no training data from this paper. The replisome structures are better used as evidence in someone else's paper than as a dataset.

effort.compute_note: Working set is the 3 mmCIF coordinate files, about 12 MB total; I measured 9NSP.cif at 3.85 MB. Peak RAM is a guess for parsing those files in Python. No cross-validation or embedding estimate is meaningful with 3 examples.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the deposited entries. One RCSB PDB search on the paper's DOI returns 3 entries, which kills the project in under a minute. I ran it.

verdict_reason: This is a cryo-electron microscopy structural paper, not a dataset. Verified against the RCSB PDB search API by DOI: the paper's complete machine-readable output is 3 structures (10WP, 9NSP, 11WZ) and 3 density maps. A5 fails by three orders of magnitude. A2 fails independently: the deposits are atomic coordinates with no outcome column, so any prediction target would have to be hand-built from figure panels in a paywalled paper that Europe PMC has no full text for. A8 fails too, because the only labels one could invent (which conformation the helicase is in) are read off the same coordinates that would serve as features. The structures are a genuine contribution to poxvirus biology and to antiviral target design, but there is nothing here to train on.
